text:
Predicates:
MountainRange(x) ::: x is a mountain range.
Location(x, y) ::: x is located in y.
Visited(x, y) ::: x visited y.
Donated(x) ::: x was donated.
Mine(x) ::: x is a mine.
Premises:
MountainRange(picuris) ∧ (Location(picuris, newMexico) ∨ Location(picuris, texas)) ::: The Picuris Mountains are a mountain range in New Mexico or Texas.
Visited(juanDeOnate, picuris) ::: Juan de Onate visited the Picuris Mountains.
Location(hardingPegmatiteMine, picuris) ∧ Donated(hardingPegmatiteMine) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine, located in the Picuris Mountains, was donated.
¬∃x (MountainRange(x) ∧ Location(x, texas) ∧ (∃y (Mine(y) ∧ Donated(y)))) ::: There are no mountain ranges in Texas that have mines which have been donated.
Conclusion:
¬∀x (Visited(juanDeOnate, x) ∧ Location(x, texas)) ::: Juan de Onate visited a mountain range in Texas.
